comparator.name: Applied Physics
comparator.sourceNotes: The formally adopted 2026-2027 programme appendix accounts for a complete 180-ECTS Applied Physics bachelor: 60 ECTS in each year. The programme has one Applied Physics major and one deepening Applied Physics minor rather than alternative named routes. Year 3 contains three restricted 5-ECTS choice groups; Atoms & Molecules, Principles of Measurement Systems, and Nanoprobing and Nanofabrication are selected by the neutral official-order tie-break. Rechecked on 2026-10-14, the public programme page still displays Mathematical Physics in its first-year summary, whereas the current formal appendix lists Differential Equations (for Physics); the formal 2026-2027 appendix governs this reconstruction. The PDF browser metadata retains a legacy '2010-2011' title, but the official TER index and every running header identify the document as the adopted 2026-2027 appendix.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum is dominated by mathematics, programming, algorithms, data, imaging, optimisation, machine learning and robotics, with a bounded energy-technology strand. The label does not claim mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum, materials, device or experimental-physics formation.

alternatives.concept: Combine mathematical and computational models with Earth-system science, geospatial and laboratory investigation, water–mineral interactions, resource recovery, climate mitigation and renewable-system assessment to study natural physical systems and sustainable technologies. This remains a related-fields route rather than an Applied Physics curriculum.

alternatives.labelRationale: Six Earth and environmental courses replace six specialist algorithmic courses, producing a natural-system, resource and energy curriculum while keeping quantitative modelling central. The label does not imply geophysics or Applied Physics equivalence.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Six courses, or 45 EC, differ in each direction. Optimisation, computer networks, algorithms, advanced algorithms, AI decision-making and reinforcement learning are replaced by Earth-system modelling, Dynamic Earth, soils and aquifers, environmental biogeochemistry, resource recovery and advanced resource research. These changes implement a natural physical-systems direction rather than threshold-filling substitutions.

alternatives.concept: Study living and human systems through molecular biology, physiology, neurobiology, laboratory work and disease mechanisms, combined with calculus, linear algebra, numerical methods, signals, probability, programming, machine learning and image analysis. This responds to medical-technology evidence through related fields, not a Medical Physics or Applied Physics curriculum.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Against the autonomous-systems route, fourteen courses (105 EC) differ in each direction; against the Earth-and-energy route, thirteen courses (97.5 EC) differ in each direction. The third programme replaces most specialist algorithms, autonomy, Earth, resource and energy study with molecular, physiological, neurobiological, laboratory and disease science, as required by the medical-technology direction.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The first programme is the strongest related quantitative and computational systems response. The renewable-energy and medical-technology evidence each supports a coherent and materially different complete route, and all three programmes pass the pairwise distinctness floor. The maximum of three alternatives is therefore reached; the separate materials and nanotechnology direction remains infeasible because UCR lacks its disciplinary and experimental sequence.

notes.text: The UCR programmes develop mathematical and computational models, autonomous systems, natural-system and renewable-energy analysis, and biomedical imaging and data perspectives. They do not reproduce mechanics and relativity, electromagnetism, optics, thermal and quantum physics, atomic and solid-state physics, electronics, materials and device physics, precision instrumentation, nanofabrication, cumulative physics laboratories or the Applied Physics research project.
